slides.title: Which Southeast Asian market first?
slides.subtitle: Market-entry recommendation for a language-learning app. The company is hypothetical; every market statistic is public World Bank data, cited on each slide.
slides.author: Head of Growth (hypothetical company)
slides.notes: The company, its budget and its team are invented for this example. The market statistics are real: World Bank World Development Indicators, last updated 2026-07-13, retrieved 2026-10-04.

slides.title: Launch in Indonesia first, and let a six-week paid test confirm it before full spend

points.headline: Indonesia is the largest reachable market
points.detail: 206M internet users in 2024, 2.4 times Vietnam's and over 3 times Thailand's.

points.headline: It stays largest after adjusting for income
points.detail: Internet users times income per person (PPP) puts Indonesia at least twice any other candidate.

points.headline: Vietnam is the best backup
points.detail: The fastest-growing economy of the four, but its online audience is 41% of Indonesia's.

points.headline: Whether we can win is still unknown
points.detail: Public statistics do not show willingness to pay, competition or acquisition cost; a six-week paid test does.

slides.source: World Bank, World Development Indicators (population, internet use, GDP per capita PPP, GDP growth), 2019-2025, retrieved 2026-10-04.
slides.notes: The answer, then the four reasons. The recommendation is conditional by design: the test decides.

slides.title: Indonesia has 206M internet users, 2.4 times Vietnam's and over 3 times Thailand's
takeaways: Indonesia has more internet users than Vietnam and Thailand combined (150M)
For a mobile app, internet users are the audience we can reach
slides.source: World Bank WDI, population (SP.POP.TOTL) and individuals using the internet, % (IT.NET.USER.ZS), 2024. Internet users = population x share online.
slides.notes: Indonesia 283.5M x 72.8% = 206.3M; Vietnam 101.0M x 84.2% = 85.0M; Philippines 115.8M x 67.3% = 77.9M; Thailand 71.7M x 90.9% = 65.1M.

slides.title: Indonesia also added the most users since 2019 (+76M) and still has 77M people offline
takeaways: Indonesia added more users in five years (76M) than Thailand has in total (65M)
Vietnam and Thailand are already mostly online, so they have less room to add users
slides.source: World Bank WDI, population and internet use (% of population), 2019 and 2024. Users = population x share online; offline = 2024 population - 2024 users.
slides.notes: Bars add up to 2024 population (rounding): Indonesia 283.5M, Philippines 115.8M, Vietnam 101.0M, Thailand 71.7M.

slides.title: Income per person in Indonesia matches Vietnam's and trails only Thailand's

exhibit.title: GDP per capita, PPP, 2024, current international $

takeaways: Indonesia and Vietnam are within 1% of each other
In 2025 Vietnam edges ahead (18,088 vs 17,660); the two remain close
The Philippines has the lowest income of the four
slides.source: World Bank WDI, GDP per capita, PPP (current international $) (NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD), 2024 and 2025.
slides.notes: PPP adjusts for local prices, which matters for a subscription priced locally.

slides.title: Adjusted for income, Indonesia's online market is at least twice that of any other candidate

exhibit.title: Internet users x GDP per capita (PPP), 2024, international $ trillion

takeaways: 2.1 times Thailand, 2.4 times Vietnam, 3.7 times the Philippines
A rough proxy used only to rank markets, not to size revenue
slides.source: World Bank WDI, 2024: internet users (population x share online) x GDP per capita, PPP. Assumes users' ability to pay tracks national income per person.
slides.notes: Indonesia 206.3M x 16,472 = 3.40T; Thailand 65.1M x 24,909 = 1.62T; Vietnam 85.0M x 16,388 = 1.39T; Philippines 77.9M x 11,814 = 0.92T.

slides.title: Vietnam is the best backup: the fastest-growing economy, but under half Indonesia's online audience
takeaways: Vietnam also grew fastest in 2025: 8.0%, against 5.1% for Indonesia
Its income per person (PPP) rose 64% from 2019 to 2025, the most of the four
But its 85M internet users are 41% of Indonesia's, so it is the backup, not the first launch
slides.source: World Bank WDI: GDP growth, annual % (NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG), mean of 2021-2025; GDP per capita, PPP (2025 / 2019 - 1); internet users 2024.
slides.notes: If the Indonesia test fails, Vietnam is next. Average growth = simple mean of the five annual values.

slides.title: Thailand is small and slow-growing, and the Philippines has the lowest income of the four

left.heading: Thailand
bullets: 91% already online, so little room for new users

right.heading: Philippines
bullets: 77.9M internet users in 2024, after a break in the series (appendix)
Smallest market after adjusting for income: $0.92T

slides.source: World Bank WDI: population, internet use, GDP per capita PPP and GDP growth, 2021-2025.
slides.notes: Thailand is richest per person but has the smallest online audience.

slides.title: We cannot yet say if we can win: app spending, competition and acquisition cost are unknown

columns: What we still have to learn

slides.source: World Bank WDI covers population, internet use and income only; the other columns list what the team must still collect.
slides.notes: Public statistics rank markets; they do not tell us whether this product wins. Owners: Strategy (spend), Growth (competition, test), Finance (payments), Legal (rules).
